note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for prostate cancer management following recent biopsy and rising PSA.

Long-standing referral for prostate cancer management. The patient is a 64-year-old active dairy farmer who lives with his partner. He reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 10/35. Medical history includes hypertension managed with valsartan, lisinopril, and metoprolol. He is an ex-smoker with a 13 pack-year history, quitting in 2015. He cycles 5 times per week as a commuter and abstains from alcohol. Recently attended a memory clinic for baseline screening, which was unremarkable. PSA has progressively risen from 3.5 ng/mL in May 2023 to 6.5 ng/mL in February 2025.
On DRE, the prostate is enlarged and nodular in the left apex, consistent with cT1c disease. General examination is unremarkable with stable vitals and no signs of metastatic disease.

admin: Lives >90 min from clinic; phone follow-up preferred where clinically safe.
